# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a mobile-first browser Canvas game called **Other House: Button Door**. Preserve the original mechanics: a 5x5 grid, center spawn, tap current or orthogonally adjacent room, reveal visited rooms, open a random event card after each accepted move, track HP and Bravery, reveal an exit through a reward event, win by stepping onto the revealed exit, and lose when HP or Bravery reaches zero.

Present the game as a Coraline-inspired button-eyed dark fantasy: a brave child in a stitched dollhouse, animated wallpaper, button moons, sewing-thread paths, needle hounds, Other Mother smiles, warm cocoa courage, seeing stones, and a moon-button door home. Use procedural Canvas/CSS art, compact portrait UI, large touch CTAs, and readable mobile HUD panels.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source Truth
The preserved source is a single-screen mobile-friendly Canvas/DOM exploration game. The player starts in the center of a default 5x5 grid, taps the current tile or an orthogonally adjacent tile, reveals visited rooms, resolves a random card event after each accepted move, tracks HP and sanity, reveals an exit through a map-style reward, wins by stepping on the revealed exit, and loses when HP or sanity reaches zero.

## Protected Mechanics
- Default grid size 5 with configurable bounds inherited from source.
- Center spawn and exit placed randomly away from spawn.
- Tap/click input on canvas only during PLAY.
- Valid move rule: orthogonal adjacent tile or self-wait; no diagonal movement.
- Event distribution: 40% neutral, 30% bad, 30% good.
- Event effects: +20 sanity/bravery capped at 100, reveal 3x3, reveal exit, -25 HP, -25 sanity/bravery, -10 sanity/bravery, or no effect.
- Win only when the exit has been revealed and the player moves onto the exit coordinate.
- Fail when HP <= 0 or sanity/bravery <= 0.
- Restart resets board, stats, inventory, exit reveal, log, and state.

## Remixed Target
Other House: Button Door reframes the same mechanic truth as a Coraline-inspired button-eyed dark fantasy dollhouse traversal. The brave child taps through stitched rooms, protects Body and Bravery, resolves domestic horror omens, reveals a moon-button door, and escapes before the Other House unravels them.

## Safe Presentation Surfaces
Canvas art, HUD wording, modal copy, background identity, particles, audio labels, fonts, color roles, feedback strip, and start/end copy are aggressively transformed while preserving state and scoring semantics.
